_source: A real 'Mathematics II Form 2 Scheme of Work' (a real Zambian secondary school's Mathematics Department; the source's own teacher name and school name are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy) was shared with this project via Drive. This is a genuine gap fill -- this app previously had no Mathematics II content for Form 2 at all. Cites the real official '2024 Mathematics II Syllabus, Ordinary Secondary Education Form 1-4' with real page citations (pp.15-20). REAL LABEL DISCREPANCY, reproduced transparently rather than silently resolved: the source file's own name says 'Term 3', but the document's own internal header explicitly states 'TERM: 2' -- trusted here over the filename, matching this app's standing practice of trusting a scheme's own internal declaration over an external label when the two disagree (e.g. mathematics_grade10.json's own Term 1 block, similarly mislabelled in its own header, resolved the same way). Filed under Term 2 accordingly. Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: Mathematics II
subject.description: Ordinary Level Secondary Mathematics II (Paper II) syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 2" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

competencies.description: Apply linear equations and inequalities in daily context (formulating, solving in one and two variables, graphical/elimination/substitution methods, inequalities and their representations)
Apply basic processes of algebra in different contexts (factorising, algebraic fractions, LCM)
Use the remainder and factor theorems in different contexts (long/synthetic division, cubic equations)

Use matrix operations in day to day activities (types, order, transposing, addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, multiplication up to order 3x3, determinants, inverse, systems of linear equations)
Apply the concept of variation in daily contexts (direct, inverse, joint and partial variation)
Use the concept of three dimensional shapes in everyday life (nets, formulae, surface area and volume of prisms, cones, pyramids, cylinders)
